data.long_meaning: Moynal is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘moon’. It is believed to be a tribute to the goddess of the moon, who is known for her nurturing and calming influence. In Hindu mythology, the moon goddess is often associated with motherhood and is revered for her ability to soothe and protect. The name Moynal carries the meaning “Moon Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Moynal usually hope their child will grow to embody moon goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Moynal, also known as Mohana or Mohana Devi, was a queen of the Chalukya dynasty in the 11th century. She is famous for her role in the construction of the Kangamba Mantapa, a beautiful pavilion inside the Shrine of Shiva at Kudala Sangama, Karnataka, India.
historical_references.context: The Chalukya Empire was a major power in South India from the 6th to the 12th century CE. Moynal, a queen of this dynasty, played an important role in the construction of a pavilion dedicated to Shiva in the 11th century CE.

historical_references.reference: Moynal, a goddess in Hindu mythology, is associated with the goddess Parvati and is believed to be the mother of Ganesha. According to legend, when Parvati was bathing, the god Shiva entered the room in disguise and disturbed her. In anger, Parvati created the god Ganesha as a guardian. When Shiva discovered this, he was pleased and granted Ganesha his elephant head. Moynal is venerated as the mother of Ganesha in Hindu devotional texts.
